description_full: Energy Recovery, Inc., together with its subsidiaries, designs, manufactures, and sells energy efficiency technology solutions in the United States, North, South and Latin America, the Middle East, Northern Africa, Asia, and Europe. It operates through Water and Emerging Technologies segments. The company offers high and low pressure, and ultra high-pressure exchangers; AT and LPT hydraulic turbochargers; and high-pressure feed and circulation pumps for use in water treatment industries, including seawater and brackish desalination, and wastewater treatment. It also provides PX G1300, which reduces energy consumption and operating costs of carbon dioxide-based refrigeration systems; and spare parts, as well as repair, field, and commissioning services. The company sells its products under the ERI, PX, PX Pressure Exchanger, Pressure Exchanger, Ultra High-Pressure PX, PX G1300, PX PowerTrain, PX G, AT, and Aquabold brands to supermarket chains, cold storage facilities, refrigeration system installers or OEMs, and other industrial users; and aftermarket customers consisting of desalination plant owners and operators. Energy Recovery, Inc. was incorporated in 1992 and is headquartered in San Leandro, California.

financial_summary: Energy Recovery, Inc. is a small-cap industrials business with a $369M market cap on $135M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +2% over the past three years and +12% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory. Operating margins are expanding by +7.7pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.

Returns on capital run at 17% against a 10% cost of capital, a 7-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it. Gross margins of 62% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $17M in free cash flow — roughly 13 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.82× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 9.2% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 2.2% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 1.6× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
